reason: Checked against the Internet Archive OCR of the T. and T. Clark, Edinburgh, 1937 first English edition (title page: translated by Ronald Gregor Smith, T. and T. Clark, 38 George Street, 1937). The sentence "All real living is meeting." stands as its own paragraph after "I become through my relation to the Thou; as I become I, I say Thou.", on the page whose running number 11 follows it (page numbers sit at the foot in this scan; 10 closes the previous page), so p. 11 holds. The translator matters here and is right: Kaufmann (1970) has "All actual life is encounter", a different rendering, and the line as given is Gregor Smith. The sentence the work is known by, so famous. Not banned, count 0, nothing shipped or near, no speaker to name. Philosophy is the form. Source line leads with the name, no dash, 76 characters. On theme.
